stories.title: Bank of Canada governor says oil‑linked inflation may return in 2027
stories.summary: Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem told the Economic Club of Canada that a second‑round effect from the recent oil price shock tied to the Middle‑East conflict is expected to add to inflation persistence in 2027, even though benchmark oil prices have fallen from recent peaks. He said businesses have largely absorbed higher production and transportation costs so far, but historical lags and business‑survey data indicate further cost pass‑through to consumers next year.
stories.why: Inflation data can shift expectations for central-bank interest rates, bond yields, borrowing costs and household purchasing power.

stories.title: Amazon acquires Decart for $7.5 billion to enhance Trainium AI chips
stories.summary: Amazon announced a $7.5 billion acquisition of Decart’s technology and team. Decart’s Optimization Stack improves AI model efficiency on non‑Nvidia hardware, and Amazon will integrate it with its Trainium processors to boost AWS AI performance. The deal follows earlier interest from Anthropic and Nvidia, and Amazon has collaborated with Decart since 2025.
stories.why: The acquisition aims to make AWS’s custom AI hardware more competitive and expand its AI‑cloud service offerings.
stories.previousTitle: Amazon acquires Decart’s AI optimization technology for $7.5 billion
stories.previousSummary: Amazon announced it will acquire Decart for $7.5 billion, obtaining the Decart Optimization Stack software that improves AI model efficiency on Nvidia, Amazon and Google hardware, along with Decart’s founding team and its AI researchers and engineers. The purchase is intended to bolster Amazon’s custom Trainium AI chips by providing a proven software layer for more efficient compute.

stories.title: Child killed by explosive ordnance in northwest Syria, UN reports near‑1,000 child casualties since Dec 2024
stories.summary: An 11‑year‑old girl, Alaa, was killed and her 10‑year‑old brother seriously injured by an explosion while tending goats in Umm Khuzaym, north‑west Syria. The BBC report says the incident, together with others this week, brings the total number of children killed or injured by explosive ordnance in Syria to nearly 1,000 since the fall of Bashar al‑Assad in December 2024, according to the UN Mine Action Service.
stories.why: It highlights the ongoing risk that unexploded ordnance poses to civilians returning to former front‑line areas.

stories.title: NATO chief says alliance will counter any space threats after reports of Russian nuclear‑armed satellite
stories.summary: NATO Secretary‑General Mark Rutte said the alliance will defend against any threats in space following German media reports that Russia is preparing to launch a nuclear‑armed satellite within 60 days. Intelligence about the possible launch was shared among NATO members earlier this month, though the source of the reports was not identified. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called the reports shocking, while Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov dismissed the stories as unverified.
stories.why: A nuclear‑armed satellite would alter the strategic balance and increase the risk of weaponising outer space.

stories.title: Tidal to ban and remove millions of AI-generated tracks as AI slop inundates music streaming
stories.summary: Tidal said it will start removing fully AI-generated music on December 9, and the process will result in more than 29 million songs being deleted from the platform by the end of the year. Tidal is also banning distribution services from delivering 100% AI-generated tracks, and will reject submissions if songs’ metadata says they are made fully using AI.
stories.why: This matters because it could change AI capabilities, costs, adoption, regulation or competitive positioning.

stories.title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei sells shares worth USD 280.41 million after IPO
stories.summary: Dario Amodei, chief executive of Anthropic, sold shares valued at USD 280.41 million following the company’s Nasdaq debut. He reported holding 202.8 million shares directly and additional shares through trusts. The IPO raised USD 81.34 billion; the stock opened above the USD 83 offering price but closed lower, still remaining above that price.
stories.why: Insider sales give investors a direct signal about the executive’s view of the company’s valuation and liquidity.
